title: Trust battery device state over UPower.onBattery
head: e9336f97ccbb
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: At exactly 100%, a Charging device is now labelled Charging while the panel treats it as full and idle
leads.consequence: A present device in Charging state, onBattery=false and percentage=1, with active rate metrics, used to render the hero text 'Fully charged' from the base modeLabel. The new Charging branch precedes the full-percentage branch and instead renders 'Charging'. But batteryFull is true from fraction >=1, charging is false, so the charging phrases and progress pulse do not run and the time/value rows are '-' despite the 'Charging' headline. UPower can deliver Charging at exactly 100%: the Linux status mapper takes 'charging' literally and the battery report only rewrites Unknown or PendingCharge at high percentages, not Charging. Consider giving the existing full-percentage rule priority for the label, or explicitly align the full/charging predicates; add a 100% Charging fixture.

leads.summary: Open #13016 conflicts on the charge-direction policy, and its kept test fails against this PR's model
leads.consequence: #13016's separate 30-second settle window calls drawingFromBattery but this PR's icon and mode label already return discharging during that window; choosing #13016's discharging binding alone would therefore show charging hero/info alongside a discharging bar icon and mode label. Both PRs also assert opposite outputs for modeLabel(Discharging, false): #13016 expects Charging and this PR expects On battery. Git reports two Panel.qml conflict hunks and one test conflict hunk against #13016's actual base; they cannot both land unchanged. This does not mean either PR alone is defective.

leads.summary: Changed tests pass even with a battery icon that never charges and a panel that never animates charging
leads.consequence: The equality checks compare two calls of the same helper but never assert different icons for charging versus discharging. The QML checks only look for substrings and still pass if the charging property adds '&& false'. A plausible regression in the exact changed outputs would get a green power test. Add a distinct-glyph assertion with known states/percentage, and an assertion of the complete charging predicate or an actual QML property exercise; use Quickshell's actual enum mapping in test data.

leads.summary: Low-battery warning is still suppressed during a discharging-on-AC condition
leads.consequence: Even while the power panel newly identifies Discharging and shows 'On battery', its service will not warn at or below 10 percent if UPower.OnBattery remains false with AC online. This service is not changed by this PR; open #11161 independently proposes removing that guard, so treat as a scope note rather than a regression in this patch.

limits: No GUI session was assigned; power QML observed by reading wiring and Node tests rather than a live bar.
Other broad GitHub search results were not all merged or diff-read; H1 is the concrete overlapping, nonstacked case fully investigated.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12259#issuecomment-5833955230) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12259#issuecomment-5842692110), checked at e9336f97. Both earlier findings are resolved. The new commit changes one label at 100% charge (below). The note about low-battery warnings is outside this PR and unchanged.

| Earlier item | Status at e9336f97 |
|---|---|
| Plug-in briefly shows "on battery" again | Resolved: the description now states the reversal of 924254ed and the plug-in window |
| Description note and panel split for `Charging` with `onBattery` still true | Resolved: the unplug-race claim is gone, and the panel now agrees with itself for that input |
| Low-battery warnings follow `UPower.onBattery` (outside this PR) | Unchanged; open PR #11161 proposes a device-state check there |

**Verified:**

- With `state=Charging` and `onBattery=true`, the icon, the mode label, the hero and the info rows all show charging. The profile argument stays `battery`, because it still follows `onBattery` as the description says. At 7159a14c the icon showed battery for this input.
- The description's account of UPower matches the UPower 1.91.4 source:
  - `OnBattery` is true only when the display state is `Discharging` and no line power is online.
  - A line-power change triggers an immediate battery refresh, followed by one-second polling for five seconds.
- The reply declines the optional charging window. Its reasoning matches the earlier review's own analysis, so nothing further is suggested for the plug-in window.
- Apart from the case below, the states listed as verified in the earlier review render as before.
- The repository power tests pass at the head and with the head merged into current `quattro` (26 assertions each). The two new assertions fail at 7159a14c.

### A full battery that reports `Charging` now says "Charging"

Input: `state=Charging`, `percentage=1`, `onBattery=false`

| Panel output | Base and 7159a14c | e9336f97 |
|---|---|---|
| Hero text (`modeLabel`) | Fully charged | Charging |
| Icon | charging-full glyph | charging-full glyph |
| Info rows | "Time to full", "Charging" (values `-`) | unchanged |
| Pulse, rotating phrases | none | none |

The new `if (d.state === states.Charging) return "Charging"` in `Model.js` runs before the `percentage >= 1` check. At 100% the panel already treats the battery as full (`batteryFull`), so `charging` is false, no phrases rotate, and the hero falls back to `modeLabel()`. UPower passes the kernel's `charging` status through at 100%. It only reclassifies `Unknown` and `PendingCharge` near full. How often real firmware reports this was not measured.

**Impact:** on hardware that reports `Charging` at 100%, the headline says "Charging" while the rest of the panel presents a full, idle battery. It is cosmetic, but it changes a settled state that showed "Fully charged" before this commit. Neither the reply nor the description mentions it.

**Suggested change:**

```js
if (d.state === states.Charging) return percentage >= 1 ? "Fully charged" : "Charging"
```

With this line, all 26 assertions pass. Across the input matrix, the only differences from 7159a14c are then the `Charging` inputs with `onBattery` still true, which is the intended fix. A test such as `modeLabel({ isPresent: true, percentage: 1, state: states.Charging }, false, states) === 'Fully charged'` would cover it.

**Optional test improvement:** the new assertion "power shows the charging icon while the battery state is charging" compares `batteryIcon` for `Charging` with `onBattery` true against `onBattery` false. It therefore also passes if both calls return the plain battery glyph. Comparing against the charging glyph, or against a `Discharging` icon at the same percentage, would catch that.

**Related open PR:** #13016 addresses the same symptom (issue #13015) with a 30-second plug-settle window. A test merge of the two heads conflicts in `Panel.qml` and `test/shell.d/power-test.sh`. Their tests also expect different results for `modeLabel(Discharging, onBattery=false)`: "On battery" here, "Charging" in #13016. If both proceed, one policy will need to be chosen.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Fresh follow-up review. Source review of e9336f97 against 7159a14c, the base and current `quattro`, plus UPower 1.91.4 and Quickshell 0.3.1 source. The repository power tests ran under Node in an isolated sandbox, at the head and at the head merged into current `quattro`. Panel binding expressions, transcribed from `Panel.qml`, were evaluated for 420 synthetic UPower input combinations per revision. The two PR heads were test-merged locally. No QML engine, live UPower, hardware or rendered panel was used, and plug-in timing was not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
